hero.h1: SaaS product redesign that modernizes your software without upsetting customers
hero.sub: A phased redesign of a live product: we fix the screens that cost you the most first, ship them in stages and keep power users productive at every step.

summary: Phased redesign of live SaaS products with an aging or inconsistent interface.
abstract: A SaaS product redesign replaces an outdated or inconsistent user interface (UI) in software that already has paying customers. Our team at ui-ux.agency audits the current product, ranks screens by business impact, builds a design system and ships the new user experience (UX) in phases over 8 to 20 weeks, so customers adapt step by step instead of all at once.

sections.h2: When does a SaaS product need a redesign?
sections.answer: A SaaS product needs a redesign when the interface, not the feature set, starts to cost sales, support time or engineering speed. These 5 signs show that point has arrived:
items: Sales demos lose to competitors with similar features and a newer interface.
Support tickets repeat for the same screens every month.
Each new feature adds another style of button, table or form.
New customers need a training call before they reach their first result.
Engineers rebuild the same component in several places because no design system exists.

sections.h2: How does our SaaS product redesign avoid a big-bang launch?
sections.answer: Our SaaS product redesign ships in phases, starting with the screens that carry the most revenue or the most support load. Customers see steady improvement instead of one sudden change.
sections.body: A big-bang redesign hides months of work and then surprises every customer on the same day. Power users lose shortcuts, saved views and habits, and support queues fill up. A phased redesign keeps the old and new interface side by side behind feature flags, invites a small group of customers to try each new area first and collects their feedback before a full rollout. The same approach works for products that started as a quick minimum viable product (MVP) build with an MVP design agency and outgrew their first interface.

sections.h2: What are the steps of a SaaS product redesign?
sections.answer: A SaaS product redesign runs in 5 steps over 8 to 20 weeks.

items.title: UX audit of the live product (2 weeks)
items.body: We review analytics, support tickets and session recordings, and interview customers and churned users.

items.title: Redesign roadmap (1 week)
items.body: We rank every area by revenue impact, support load and effort, and agree the release phases.

items.title: Design system first (2–4 weeks)
items.body: New navigation, typography, colours and components that engineers adopt before any screen changes.

items.title: Phase-by-phase design (4–10 weeks)
items.body: We redesign one area at a time, test it with existing customers and hand it over for build.

items.title: Beta and rollout (ongoing)
items.body: A beta group uses each new area first; we fix issues before the full release.

sections.h2: SaaS product redesign vs a visual refresh
sections.answer: A visual refresh changes how the product looks; a SaaS product redesign changes how it works. The right choice depends on where customers struggle today.

sections.h2: What results does a SaaS product redesign target?
sections.answer: Every SaaS product redesign we run targets 4 results, each measured against the numbers before the redesign.

items.title: Fewer support tickets
items.body: Clearer screens and error messages cut repeat questions about the same features.

items.title: Faster onboarding
items.body: New customers reach their first result without a training call.

items.title: Stronger sales demos
items.body: A modern, consistent interface helps the sales team win evaluations.

items.title: Faster engineering
items.body: A shared design system means engineers reuse components instead of rebuilding them.

sections.h2: How much does a SaaS product redesign cost?
sections.answer: A SaaS product redesign costs $50,000 to $200,000 and runs for 8 to 20 weeks. The number of screens, user roles and release phases decides where a project sits in that range.
sections.body: A redesign of navigation, dashboard and one core workflow sits near $50,000. A full platform with an admin area, reporting, a design system and a mobile app sits near $200,000. Products that need a new feature set as well as a new interface work with our SaaS design agency team. All price factors are listed in the UI UX design cost guide.

sections.answer: Answers to common questions about redesigning a live SaaS product.

faqs.q: Will customers lose features during a SaaS product redesign?
faqs.a: No. We map every existing feature before design starts, and each phase keeps or improves it; nothing is removed without data and customer input.

faqs.q: Can we keep our current front-end framework?
faqs.a: Yes. The design system is built to match your current React, Angular or Vue setup, so engineers adopt it gradually.

faqs.q: How do you tell customers about the redesign?
faqs.a: We design in-app announcements, a short tour of each new area and an optional switch back to the old view during the beta.

faqs.q: Is a SaaS product redesign worth it for a small team?
faqs.a: Yes, when support load or lost deals trace back to the interface. Start with a 2-week audit; it shows whether a full redesign pays back.
